newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Public support for EMU up in 1996 - EU survey.
newsitem.headline: Public support for EMU up in 1996 - EU survey.

text.p: The public is more positive towards monetary union in all European Union member states except France, Finland and Britain, according to a survey published on Thursday.
"Since the announcement in December 1995 of the name of the new European currency, public debate concerning its introduction has intensified," the survey, conducted last October and November, said.
"The increased awareness has resulted in an overall increase in support for the single currency," the survey, published by the European Commission, added.
A survey in the autumn of 1995 showed 47 percent for the single currency and 33 percent against.

"The current survey, conducted twelve months later, shows support at 51 percent, while the 'against' figure remained at 33 percent," it said, adding that the figures were similar to the spring survey in 1996.
The support was the highest in Italy, 73 percent for and only 11 percent against, giving a positive "net result" of 62 points.
Most opponents were found in Finland, Britain, Sweden and Denmark. Those against EMU in those four contries far outnumbered those in favour.

The survey said net gains were recorded in all member states but three. The net result, the difference between those for and against, fell by 10 percentage points to 25 in France, by seven to minus 27 in Finland and by one to minus 26 in Britain.
In contrast, there was a net gain of 14 points in Austria and 12 points in Greece.
In Germany, 39 percent were for EMU while 42 percent were against. No comparison was given. -- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11
